column1: What is the fundamental limitation of JavaScript's native Object.freeze() method?
column2: Object.freeze() is shallow; nested objects and nested arrays remain completely mutable unless explicitly frozen.

column1: How do you create an immutable nested object array in vanilla JavaScript?
column2: Call Object.freeze() on the outer array and wrap each inner object element in Object.freeze().

column1: In strict mode ('use strict'), what happens when attempting to mutate a property of an Object.freeze() object?
column2: The JavaScript engine throws a TypeError: Cannot assign to read only property.

column1: In non-strict mode, what happens when attempting to mutate an Object.freeze() object?
column2: The mutation fails silently without throwing an error, and the object remains unchanged.

column2: Decoded images in browser GPU/RAM allocate memory based on uncompressed pixel dimensions (width × height × 4 bytes per pixel for RGBA), not file size on disk.

column1: What is the primary benefit of maintaining thumbnail and fullImage properties in PORTFOLIO_DATA after adding the images array?
column2: Backward compatibility, ensuring existing UI components (like grid cards) continue rendering without breaking before they are upgraded.

column2: Array.prototype.find().

column2: Array.prototype.findIndex().

column1: What does Object.isSealed(obj) check compared to Object.isFrozen(obj)?
column2: Object.isSealed() allows modifying existing property values (only prevents adding/deleting properties), whereas Object.isFrozen() also makes all existing properties read-only (writable: false).

column1: Why should captions and alt descriptions be modeled directly alongside image URLs in the data schema?
column2: It enforces accessibility (A11y) parity and provides rich, contextual metadata for screen readers and UI captions.

column1: How does optimizing image asset dimensions improve Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)?
column2: Smaller file sizes reduce network download time, and smaller pixel dimensions reduce browser main-thread image decoding and paint time.

column1: What browser property on the HTMLImageElement interface indicates whether an image has completed downloading and decoding?
column2: img.complete (boolean true or false).

column1: What event fires on an element when its raster data finishes loading successfully into the DOM?
column2: The load event.

column1: What event fires on an element if the image URL is broken or fails to download?
column2: The error event.

column1: Why is client-side data immutability critical in single-page applications without frameworks?
column2: It prevents accidental side-effect mutations across independent components (e.g. filters, modals, sliders) sharing the same state.

column1: What is the time complexity of searching an item by id in an array of N objects using Array.prototype.find()?
column2: O(N) linear time complexity.

column1: How can you look up an object by id in O(1) constant time instead of O(N) linear time?
column2: By storing or indexing the objects in a JavaScript Map or a hash object keyed by id.
